title: ORLIS: Obfuscation-Resilient Library Detection for Android
venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Mobile Software Engineering and Systems (MOBILESoft)
detection_method: Two-stage approach: (1) sdhash over interprocedural method/class features to narrow candidate libraries; (2) ssdeep class digests and injective app-class to library-class mapping
module_decoupling: None explicit — operates on decompiled app classes matched against library class profiles; no separate module decoupling phase
features_used: interprocedural call-graph and class-hierarchy-derived method/class features
sdhash similarity digests for app-to-library candidate filtering
ssdeep class digests for injective class correspondence
matching_algorithm: Stage 1 compares application and library digests to produce a small candidate set. Stage 2 sorts class-pair similarities and greedily constructs an injective mapping, so at most one application class maps to a library class.
obfuscation_handling: Replaces obfuscation-sensitive identifiers and uses interprocedural call relationships and class hierarchy information expected to survive common renaming-oriented obfuscation.
r8_resilience: Not tested (pre-R8 era; tested on Allatori and ProGuard obfuscation)
version_level_f1: Not reported — no version-level detection metrics
speed: ~1,438s per app (slowest among all evaluated tools)
dataset_size: FDroidData contains 659 obfuscated app builds derived from 282 source projects and 453 unique library jars; LibDetectData uses 7,519 available library jars from the prior benchmark.
partial_lib_handling: Yes — class-level similarity and injective mapping can report the subset of library classes matched in an application.
open_source: Not confirmed publicly available; requires Soot environment (difficult installation)
transitive_deps: No — does not handle transitive dependencies
strengths: Uses interprocedural structural features for obfuscation resilience
Reports 0.71 precision, 0.63 recall, and 0.67 F1 on FDroidData
Injective class mapping supports partial-inclusion analysis
Two-stage architecture (fast filter + deep check) is a reusable design pattern
Evaluates both source-grounded F-Droid builds and a prior closed-source benchmark
weaknesses: Extremely slow (~1,438s/app) — prohibitive for large-scale analysis
Lowest library-level F1 among Gen-1 tools (~62-67%)
impact_on_project: ORLIS demonstrates that call-graph-derived features and class correspondence can support obfuscation-resilient partial inclusion, but the analysis cost is high. Its reusable lesson is the two-stage architecture: sdhash candidate filtering followed by ssdeep-based injective class mapping. It does not provide exact-version or standard SBOM authority, so its output should be treated as structural identity evidence rather than a final package/version claim.
